name: Wyoming
keyNotes: 4-year redemption is the LONGEST in the US — capital is tied up
15% fixed rate compensates for long hold
Low population state — limited inventory but less competition
summary: Wyoming holds annual tax lien sales in November. 4-year redemption. Inventory dominated by energy sector and agricultural land. Statute: WS §39-13-108.
typeWhy: Wyoming sells tax lien certificates at annual November sales. The investor holds the lien while the owner retains title during the 4-year redemption period — one of the longest in the country. WS §39-13-108.
rateWhy: Wyoming sets a fixed statutory rate of 15% per annum on tax lien certificates. This higher-than-average rate compensates for the exceptionally long 4-year redemption period. WS §39-13-108.
notBeginnerReason: 4-year redemption, limited inventory, November-only auctions, and primarily rural energy/agricultural land.
beginnerTip: Laramie and Natrona counties have the best WY inventory. The 4-year redemption makes Wyoming a very long-term play — not recommended unless you understand the energy land market.
risks: 4-year redemption — among the longest in lien states
Energy sector land has specialized valuation considerations
ddExtra: Verify mineral rights status — commonly separated from surface rights in Wyoming
Calculate opportunity cost over 4-year holding period
Confirm the November sale date with the county treasurer by October

steps: Find your target county treasurer at wyoming.gov/government/counties
Contact the treasurer in September to confirm the November sale schedule
Register in person — most WY counties do not have online bidding

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

rules.statute: WS §39-13-108 (Enforcement — Tax Lien Sale, Redemption, Deed)

process.step1: Taxes delinquent. County treasurer publishes notice in local newspaper 3 consecutive weeks prior to sale.
process.step2: Annual public auction. Purchaser pays all taxes + interest + costs. County issues Certificate of Purchase.
process.step3: County retains physical custody of Certificate. Sends copy to purchaser within reasonable time.
process.step4: During 4-year redemption: original owner may redeem. Purchaser may pay subsequent taxes (also earn 15%/yr).
process.step5: 4 years post-sale: cert holder may apply for tax deed (providing statutory notice). County treasurer issues deed.
process.step6: 6-year limit: tax deed CANNOT be issued after 6 years from original sale date. Certificate void.

auction.frequency: Annual — last Thursday in July OR first Thursday in August
auction.platform: In-person county courthouse/designated location. Each of 23 counties independently.
auction.bidMethod: Premium bid — purchaser bids and pays full amount of taxes + interest + costs
auction.registration: Pre-registration varies by county. Some: day of sale 8 AM. Teton: must pre-register. W-9 required at many counties.
auction.payment: Cash, bank checks, credit/debit cards (county-dependent). No personal checks at most counties.
auction.limitation: Some counties cap attendance (Teton: pre-registered only, Lincoln: 100 max)

otc.name: County-Held Certificates (OTC)
otc.process: If no bidder at tax sale — county holds certificate. Contact county treasurer to purchase county-held liens.
otc.note: County-held certs earn same 15%/yr rate upon redemption

subTax.name: Subsequent Tax Payments
subTax.rate: 15% per annum on subsequent taxes paid
subTax.obligation: Certificate holder is under NO obligation to pay subsequent taxes. Optional.
subTax.note: If paid — subsequent taxes attach to original lien and earn 15%/yr

redemption.period: 4 years from date of tax lien sale
redemption.window: Can redeem anytime until county treasurer accepts tax deed application (between 4–6 years)
redemption.amounts: Amount of tax sold at sale + 3% penalty + 15% simple interest + any subsequent taxes paid by cert holder with 15% interest + redemption fee + purchaser's actual expenses (not to exceed $250 if redeeming after pre-deed notice)

deedPath.name: Treasurer's Deed
deedPath.eligibleWindow: 4 years to 6 years from date of sale
deedPath.noticeRequired: Cert holder must comply with statutory notice requirements BEFORE applying. 60-day notice to record owner + mortgage holders by personal service or certified mail.
deedPath.taxDeedAfter6yr: ⚡ Tax deed CANNOT be issued after 6 years from sale. Certificate expires. All money invested is potentially lost.
deedPath.titleEffect: Deed conveys title free and clear. 6-year SOL on actions to recover property (WS §39-13-108(c)(D))

surplus.name: Surplus Proceeds
surplus.statute: WS §39-13-108 — surplus of personal property sale returned to owner. Tyler v. Hennepin applies to real property.
surplus.process: Surplus from sale above taxes + costs returned to former owner. Tyler v. Hennepin constitutional requirement.
surplus.note: WY statute §39-13-108(A)(V) explicitly requires surplus return on personal property distraint — Tyler applies to real property surplus.

es.summary: Wyoming realiza ventas anuales de gravámenes fiscales en noviembre. Redención de 4 años. El inventario está dominado por tierra del sector energético y agrícola. Estatuto: WS §39-13-108.
es.typeWhy: Wyoming es un estado de gravamen porque los condados venden certificados de gravamen fiscal en noviembre con período de redención de 4 años — uno de los más largos del país (WS §39-13-108).
es.rateWhy: La tasa del 15% es atractiva pero la redención de 4 años es una de las más largas del país, inmovilizando capital en un mercado dominado por tierra del sector energético y agrícola (WS §39-13-108).
es.notBeginnerReason: Redención de 4 años, inventario limitado, subastas solo en noviembre y tierra predominantemente de sector energético/agrícola.
es.beginnerTip: Los condados Laramie y Natrona tienen el mejor inventario de WY. La redención de 4 años hace que Wyoming sea una estrategia a muy largo plazo — no se recomienda a menos que entienda el mercado de tierra energética.
risks: Redención de 4 años — entre las más largas en estados de gravamen
La tierra del sector energético tiene consideraciones de valoración especializadas
Las subastas solo en noviembre limitan el tiempo
ddExtra: Verifique el estado de los derechos minerales — comúnmente separados de los derechos de superficie en Wyoming
Calcule el costo de oportunidad durante el período de retención de 4 años
Confirme la fecha de venta de noviembre con el tesorero del condado para octubre

steps: Encuentre al tesorero de su condado en wyoming.gov/government/counties
Contacte al tesorero en septiembre para confirmar el calendario de venta de noviembre
Solicite la lista de propiedades en mora
Regístrese en persona — la mayoría de los condados de WY no tienen pujas en línea
